public_rationale: May 2025 tests documented frequent illegal moves in o3 and o4-mini games [e1]. September 2023 tests of gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct reported a median game length of 44 moves and 0.3% illegal outputs, showing substantial variation between tested models [e2]. Neither report establishes the chess phase of first illegal moves or an engine-scored decline in move quality from opening to middlegame [e1, e2]. The combined claim therefore remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: Aggregate game lengths do not identify when the middlegame begins or when failures occur relative to it [e1, e2].
The May report stops games at the first illegal output, includes two notation-ambiguity cases, and has inconsistent subsidiary counts [e1].
Extended legal play in one model does not establish how often the claimed pattern occurs across relevant models [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs often get lost by the chess midgame, playing worse and making illegal moves.

statement.excerpt: So what happens? By the midgame, LLMs often get lost. Not only does the quality of play diminish deeper into the game, but LLMs start to make illegal moves.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

from_speaker: quality of play diminish deeper into the game
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a recurring pattern across relevant LLM games: deterioration in move quality and illegal moves appearing by the middlegame.
Often does not mean every model or every game. An isolated failure is insufficient.
Middlegame means the chess phase following the opening, not an evaluator-imposed move number.
Move quality and legality must be assessed separately. This claim does not require proving the proposed world-model explanation.
The target is the performance of relevant models as known by publication, including applicable earlier tests. There is no June-only cutoff.
criteria.support_condition: Repeated-game evaluations show that illegal moves commonly occur by the middlegame and that independently scored move quality declines from the opening into later play across relevant models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative stage-specific evaluations show generally maintained or improved move quality and consistently legal play through the middlegame. An exceptional successful model alone does not refute often.

evidence.explanation: Frequent illegal endings and reported median lengths around 15 moves support recurring early failures in these configurations. The study does not supply a controlled phase-specific decline in move quality, and its game-count summaries contain inconsistencies.

evidence.excerpt: the ability to play legal moves.
evidence.locator: Conclusion about ability of gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct to play legal moves
evidence.explanation: For gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, the report describes extended legal play, a median game length of 44 moves and 0.3% illegal outputs. This limits generalization across LLMs, but neither disproves often nor establishes stable move quality by phase.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reproducible evaluation of models existing by June 28, 2025 that labels chess phases, reports first illegal moves separately from notation errors, and compares engine-scored move quality across phases while accounting for games stopped at the first illegal move.
